description:
Company Overview:

We are building Protege to solve the biggest unmet need in AI — getting access to the right training data. The process today is time intensive, incredibly expensive, and often ends in failure. The Protege platform facilitates the secure, efficient, and privacy-centric exchange of AI training data.

Solving AI’s data problem is a generational opportunity. We’re backed by world-class investors and already powering partnerships with some of the most ambitious teams in AI. The company that succeeds will be one of the largest in AI — and in tech.

We’re a lean, fast-moving, high-trust team of builders who are obsessed with velocity and impact. Our culture is built for people who thrive on ambiguity, own outcomes, and want to shape the future of data and AI.

The role

Protege is hiring a Staff Software Engineer to build and operate the transformation layer of our data platform — the pipelines that take ingested, sensitive source data and turn it into de-identified, delivery-ready datasets. This is a hands-on, data-engineering-oriented software role with end-to-end ownership of the jobs that transform, protect, and package data at scale.

Protege connects organizations that hold high-value data with the AI builders who need it. Much of that data is regulated healthcare data. Before any of it reaches a customer, it passes through a transformation pipeline that de-identifies it to a defensible standard, preserves its analytical value, and packages it for delivery. The quality, correctness, and auditability of that pipeline is what makes the exchange possible.

You’ll work on a small team alongside a senior engineer who owns much of today’s transform logic, and you’ll partner closely with privacy, solutions, and ingestion teams. The work spans distributed Spark jobs, configuration-driven transform frameworks, free-text processing, and the operational discipline required when the input is privacy-protected. This role is ideal for engineers who like precise, high-stakes data work, want deep ownership of a critical system, and enjoy turning one-off requests into reusable, well-tested capabilities.

What you'll do

  • Build and extend the de-identification transform framework. Extend Protege’s capabilities by building composable transform chains, and developing multi-modal processes.

  • Maintain the boundary between protected and de-identified data. You own the guards between protected and de-identified data, extend them as new workflows need to cross the boundary, and make sure every crossing stays validated and auditable.

  • Develop agentic workflows in the pipeline. You bring ideas for where agents and models fit in our transformation layer and build them into production with the evaluation and guardrails PHI requires.

  • Make jobs self-serve for solutions engineers. Clear interfaces, sensible defaults, and runbooks let non-owners run transforms correctly without escalating to the team.

  • Turn recurring one-off requests into reusable capabilities. Deal-specific transform or packaging work becomes a job mode, shared utility, or config option rather than a fork.

What success looks like

  • 30 days: Mapped the flow from ingestion through de-identification to delivery, met the privacy, solutions, ingestion, and catalog partners, and shipped an update to the transform pipeline that adds a capability or makes an existing job easier to run.

  • 60 days: Created a new transform from a privacy or solutions request, including its config, tests, documentation, and a measured quality check, and seen it run on real provider data.

  • 90 days: Owning the transform pipeline end to end, including its configs, operations, and support; proposing and developing improvements to its reliability, usability, or development speed, with at least one in production.

What you'll bring

  • You have written Python libraries or frameworks that other engineers depend on, with tests and documentation.

  • You have shipped data pipelines on AWS and made the storage, compute, and access-control decisions yourself.

  • You have turned a vague data request into a precise, tested implementation.

  • You have built internal tools that serve a range of end-users.

  • Nice to have: hands-on Databricks experience (Delta tables, Unity Catalog or a comparable governance layer).

  • Nice to have: text processing at scale (regex or NLP pipelines), workflow orchestration (Dagster, Airflow), or config-driven data frameworks.

What to expect

  1. Recruiter screen (30 min)

  2. Conversation with the hiring manager (45 min)

  3. Technical Interview (60 min)

  4. Work Trial (4 hrs)

  5. Conversation with VP Eng (30 min)

  6. Conversation with CEO (30 min)
